\caption{Post hoc resampling constructions of $R$ (exploratory). The first row was designated as the post hoc construction before it was computed (amendment 16); the others are sensitivity analyses, none planned before the result. Interval: the 90\,\% Fieller interval from the covariance of the resampled change in Brier score $\Delta$ and baseline gain $D$, with a normal critical value; its upper end is a one-sided 95\,\% limit only if the resampling is valid, which the few clusters do not ensure. $\hat D/\mathrm{SE}$: the baseline gain over its resampling standard error. $\nu$: the Satterthwaite effective number of clusters for $L_+=\Delta-\theta D$ at the upper end $\theta$; upper ends with $z$ and $t(\nu-1)$ critical values; ``none'': no finite end at that critical value, or $\nu-1<1$. In the protocol's simulations the $t(\nu-1)$ end, when it existed, always exceeded the true value, but it existed in about one replicate in ten (Table~\STabSeventeenCov{} of the Supplement). Units: the resampled clusters (for (c) and (d), countries; for the pigeonhole bootstrap, the smaller of the two factors; location groups and activations are mostly nested or overlapping, where the pigeonhole bootstrap is expected to be conservative). Split and reading: the primary split or the split that keeps activations whole, with the frozen reading of the protocol or the corrected reading of Norwegian names.
